extraction.name: RoboFAC dataset
extraction.description: RoboFAC is a robotic failure question-answering dataset for robot manipulation videos. It comprises 9,440 erroneous manipulation trajectories and 78,623 QA pairs across 16 diverse tasks and 53 scenes in both simulation and real-world environments, covering six failure types for task understanding, failure analysis, and failure correction.
extraction.creator: Weifeng Lu; Minghao Ye; Zewei Ye; Ruihan Tao; Shuo Yang; Bo Zhao
extraction.citeAs: Weifeng Lu, Minghao Ye, Zewei Ye, Ruihan Tao, Shuo Yang, and Bo Zhao. RoboFAC: A Comprehensive Framework for Robotic Failure Analysis and Correction. arXiv:2505.12224, 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed by collecting simulation data for 14 robotic tasks in the ManiSkill environment, augmented with objects from the YCB Object Dataset and scenes from ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR; failure data were generated by replacing the original expert policy with a code snippet that generates an erroneous trajectory at a selected substage. Real-world data were collected for 6 tasks via teleoperation using the SO-100 robotic arm.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Software Collection; Experiments; Manual Human Curator; Direct measurement
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Given the motion planning for the robotic arm occasionally failed, resulting in trajectories that did not align with the corresponding textual descriptions, we manually performed thorough data cleaning and retained approximately 75% of the collected data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Simulation data for 14 robotic tasks in the ManiSkill environment, augmented with objects from the YCB Object Dataset and scenes from ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR; recorded robotic failure videos with corresponding descriptive text; real-world videos collected for 6 tasks via teleoperation using the SO-100 robotic arm.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The raw data were annotated to construct video-based QA samples for eight question types; for each question type, five question templates were provided. For each sample, reference answers for task identification, task planning, failure detection, failure identification, and failure locating were directly extracted from the textual description associated with the video, while failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction answers were generated using both the video and its corresponding textual description as inputs to GPT-4o, and all GPT-4o outputs were manually reviewed and corrected.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For five question types, reference answers were directly extracted from the textual description associated with the video; for the remaining three types, GPT-4o generated reference answers from the video and textual description, and all outputs from GPT-4o were manually reviewed and corrected.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The current integration of the model into the VLA-controlled robotic system is not yet seamless; the work applies the model exclusively to the VLA model; the success rate remains subject to further enhancement, largely due to the VLA model’s limited ability to follow complex natural language instructions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: This enables more robust and transparent deployment of vision-language models in diverse and challenging robotic manipulation scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: robotic failure video understanding; task understanding, failure analysis, and failure correction based on robot video; serving as an external critic to assist VLA models in recovering from failures in real-world robotic control tasks
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: To generate failure data, we replace the original expert policy with a code snippet that generates an erroneous trajectory at the selected substage, causing the overall robotic task to fail. To prevent models from overfitting to failure patterns, we also collect 1,160 successful trajectories from simulation and 122 successful trajectories from real-world executions. Specifically, we randomly sample 60K QA pairs from the simulated RoboFAC dataset as the training set. The remaining QA pairs are used for evaluation, including 10K simulated QA pairs and 8K QA pairs from real-world data.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Given the motion planning for the robotic arm occasionally failed, resulting in trajectories that did not align with the corresponding textual descriptions, we manually performed thorough data cleaning and retained approximately 75% of the collected data.
